docs.title: Welcome to Zhiva
docs.text:
Zhiva is a lightweight framework for building cross-platform desktop applications with HTML, CSS and TypeScript. It uses the system webview and the Bun runtime instead of bundling a browser and Node.js, so applications stay small and start fast.

The backend is a normal Bun process, the frontend is served by a local HTTP server, and the two communicate through a small authenticated REST API instead of IPC.

docs.title: 1. Install Zhiva
docs.text:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wxn0brP/Zhiva/HEAD/install/prepare.sh | bash
export PATH="$HOME/.zhiva/bin:$PATH"

On Windows, use the installer.

docs.title: 2. Install an application
docs.text:
zhiva install Zhiva-store-app
zhiva start Zhiva-store-app

docs.title: 3. Create your own application
docs.text:
zhiva create my-app
cd my-app
bun run build
zhiva start .

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• System webview: uses WebKitGTK on Linux and WebView2 on Windows, without a bundled Chromium.
  • Bun backend: TypeScript runs natively, without a build step on the server side.
  • REST instead of IPC: the frontend calls apiRouter endpoints with helpers from base-lib.
  • Git-based distribution: applications are regular Git repositories, installed and updated with the CLI.
  • Static and URL modes: serve a built SPA, or wrap an existing website in a window.
  • Shared runtime: the engine, base-lib and dependencies are installed once in ~/.zhiva.

docs.title: Platform Support
docs.text:
• Linux: supported. Requires WebKitGTK 4.1 and GTK 3.
  • Windows: supported. Requires the WebView2 runtime.
  • macOS: the implementation exists but is untested on real hardware.

Zhiva is an experimental project. It is used for tools, utilities, prototypes and internal applications.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
Zhiva applications have two sides:

  • backend (src/index.ts), a Bun process that imports @wxn0brp/zhiva-base-lib/server and @wxn0brp/zhiva-base-lib/api,
  • frontend (src/browser.ts), compiled JavaScript running in the webview, which imports @wxn0brp/zhiva-base-lib/front/api.

They communicate through a local HTTP server. The frontend never talks to the backend directly; the native engine loads a local URL with a secret token attached.

docs.title: Imports
docs.text:
import { app, oneWindow, waitToStart, port } from "@wxn0brp/zhiva-base-lib/server";
import { apiRouter, apiSecret } from "@wxn0brp/zhiva-base-lib/api";

The package root re-exports the server module, so import { app } from "@wxn0brp/zhiva-base-lib" is equivalent.

docs.title: app
docs.text:
A Falcon Frame instance.

app.static("public");                         // serve ./public at /
app.static("/assets", "./dist/assets");       // serve a directory under a path
app.static("dist", {
    errorIfDirNotFound: false,
});

Other methods used by applications:

Method Purpose app.static(url, dir?, options?) Serve a directory app.get(url, handler) Define a route on the main server app.use(url, middleware) Mount middleware app.setVar(name, value) Set a Falcon Frame variable, e.g. a layout app.getApp() Access the underlying server

apiRouter is mounted automatically at /zhiva-api.

docs.title: apiRouter
docs.text:
A Falcon Frame Router for authenticated endpoints.

apiRouter.get("/notes", async req => {
    return { err: false, notes: [] };
});

apiRouter.post("/notes", async req => {
    return { err: false, note: req.body };
});

Handlers can return:

  • an object, sent as a JSON response,
  • a string, sent as a text response,
  • undefined, in which case you should use res directly (res.status(500).send(...)).

Recommended response shape:

{ err: boolean, msg?: string, code?: string, ...data }

A request without the x-zhiva-token header receives:

{ "err": true, "msg": "Unauthorized", "code": "UNAUTHORIZED" }

with HTTP status 401.

docs.title: oneWindow(path?, title?)
docs.text:
Creates the application window after the server starts.

await oneWindow();
await oneWindow("/settings", "Settings");
  • path defaults to /.
  • title is optional; the window also tracks document.title changes.
  • Closing the window ends the process.
  • If the native engine cannot start, Zhiva shows a notification and opens the URL in the default browser.

docs.title: Server lifecycle and ports
docs.text:
The server binds to 127.0.0.1. The port comes from, in order:

  1. forcePort in zhiva.json,
  2. the last port stored in .zhiva-port in the application directory,
  3. ZHIVA_PORT,
  4. a random free port.

Because the saved port wins over ZHIVA_PORT, use forcePort to pin a port, or remove .zhiva-port after changing the variable. If the preferred port is taken, the server falls back to a random one.

docs.title: Imports
docs.text:
import {
    fetchApi,
    fetchApiJson,
    fetchApiPost,
    zhivaApiToken,
} from "@wxn0brp/zhiva-base-lib/front/api";

import { isZhiva } from "@wxn0brp/zhiva-base-lib/front/utils";

docs.title: fetchApi(url, opts?, query?)
docs.text:
Fetches /zhiva-api/<url> and adds the x-zhiva-token header.

const response = await fetchApi("notes", {}, { limit: "10" });
const data = await response.json();
  • url is relative to /zhiva-api/.
  • query values are stringified and appended to the URL.
  • The returned value is a normal Response, without error handling.

docs.title: fetchApiJson<T>(url, opts?, query?)
docs.text:
Parses the response as JSON and types it:

interface NotesResponse {
    err: boolean;
    notes: string[];
}

const data = await fetchApiJson<NotesResponse>("notes");

docs.title: fetchApiPost<T>(url, body?, opts?, query?)
docs.text:
Sends a JSON POST and parses the response:

const result = await fetchApiPost<{ err: boolean; id: string }>("notes", {
    text: "hello",
});

fetchApiJson and fetchApiPost do not throw on HTTP errors or on err: true. Check the err field yourself, or wrap the call.

docs.title: Token
docs.text:
The token is generated per process with crypto.randomBytes, and the frontend receives it in the window URL as the zhiva-secret query parameter. fetchApi reads it automatically and exposes it as zhivaApiToken.

Do not log the token, copy it into other origins or put it in a URL of a remote page. The token only protects the local API, it is not an account credential.

docs.title: Window bindings
docs.text:
The native engine exposes asynchronous functions on window, available only inside Zhiva:

Binding Purpose zhiva_isApp Returns whether the page runs in Zhiva zhiva_closeApp() Closes the window and exits the process zhiva_setWindowTitle(title) Sets the window title zhiva_openExternal(url) Opens a URL in the system browser zhiva_echo(value) Debug helper that prints to the backend log

The engine also:

  • updates the window title when document.title changes,
  • opens <a target="_blank"> links in the system browser.

Use isZhiva from @wxn0brp/zhiva-base-lib/front/utils instead of checking the globals directly.

There are no TypeScript wrappers for the bindings yet. When you call them, guard for their presence:

const openExternal = (window as any).zhiva_openExternal;
if (typeof openExternal === "function") await openExternal(url);

docs.title: Security model
docs.text:
• Only the local server is exposed, on 127.0.0.1.
  • Every apiRouter route requires the token, even in development, unless ZHIVA_DEVELOPMENT_DISABLE_SECURE_TOKEN=I KNOW WHAT I AM DOING is set.
  • The token is per process, not per user.
  • Applications run with the full permissions of the user who started them. Install only repositories you trust.

docs.title: Application Types
docs.text:
Zhiva supports three kinds of applications. The mode is selected in zhiva.json; the checks run in this order:

  1. static is present: static server, no backend process,
  2. url is present: the window loads a remote URL,
  3. neither: full-stack mode, Zhiva runs the start script from package.json.

static and url are mutually exclusive. name is required by the schema.

docs.title: 1. Full-stack (default)
docs.text:
The application runs a Bun backend, usually with base-lib, and the window loads the local server.

  • Use cases: local databases, file system access, shell commands, authenticated APIs, persistent state.
  • Requirements: package.json with a start script, zhiva.json with a name.
  • Communication: an authenticated REST API through apiRouter.

A minimal backend:

import { app, oneWindow } from "@wxn0brp/zhiva-base-lib/server";
import { apiRouter } from "@wxn0brp/zhiva-base-lib/api";

app.static("public");
app.static("dist");

apiRouter.get("/hello", async () => {
    return { err: false, msg: "Hello world!" };
});

oneWindow();

The frontend calls fetchApiJson("hello"). See API Reference and Development.

docs.title: 2. Static-only
docs.text:
Zhiva serves built files with its own server. No application backend is started, so there is no apiRouter and no API token.

  • Use cases: SPAs built with Vite, React, Vue, Svelte or Angular, documentation sites, static tools.
  • Configuration: the static object in zhiva.json.
{
    "name": "My Static App",
    "icon": "./public/icon.png",
    "static": {
        "dirs": {
            "/": "./public",
            "-/": "./dist",
            "/assets": "./dist/assets"
        },
        "files": {
            "/config.js": "./src/config.js"
        },
        "redirects": {
            "/old": "/new"
        }
    }
}
  • dirs: maps URL paths to directories. If omitted, Zhiva serves . at /.
  • Negative prefixes (-/) allow several directories to share the same URL root; the leading dashes are stripped.
  • files: maps a URL to a single file.
  • redirects: maps a URL to a redirect target.
  • vars: Falcon Frame variables, for example { "layout": "public/layout.html" }.

Assemble the build output yourself and point dirs at it. Installation still runs bun install --production and the build script when package.json defines them, so you can build the assets during install instead of committing dist/; if you do not define a build step, commit the built files.

docs.title: 3. URL-based
docs.text:
The window loads a remote website. No local server, no API, no token.

  • Use cases: wrapping an existing web application or service in a window.
  • Configuration: the url field in zhiva.json.
{
    "name": "My Wrapped App",
    "icon": "./assets/icon.png",
    "url": "https://example.com"
}

The page runs with the permissions of the remote site, not of a Zhiva application. Window bindings such as zhiva_closeApp and zhiva_openExternal are still injected, but the site may not use them. If the native engine is unavailable, the URL opens in the default browser.

docs.title: Choosing a mode
docs.text:
Requirement Mode Local files, database, shell commands Full-stack Existing static build, no backend Static Existing website, no local code URL

For a new project, start with zhiva create, which generates a full-stack application. Remove the backend only when you are sure the app needs no server-side logic.

docs.title: Zhiva Architecture
docs.text: Zhiva is split into small repositories with separate responsibilities.

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text: Repository Role Zhiva Documentation, installer and project coordination Zhiva-scripts The zhiva CLI Zhiva-native Native engine: window, webview, system integration Zhiva-base-lib Server, API router and frontend helpers Zhiva-template-app Application template Zhiva-store-app Application store Zhiva-registry Verified and banned application lists Zhiva-page Website

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
1. The native engine: a C++ executable using a system webview (WebKitGTK on Linux, WebView2 on Windows). It creates the window, injects the zhiva_* bindings, handles the window title and opens external links.
  2. The CLI (zhiva): installs, updates and starts applications. It also manages the engine, dependencies, shortcuts and the local database.
  3. The Base Library (base-lib): a TypeScript library imported by applications. It provides a Falcon Frame server, an authenticated apiRouter and frontend fetch helpers.
  4. The application: a Git repository with zhiva.json, a frontend and, optionally, a Bun backend.

docs.title: Startup flow
docs.text:
1. zhiva start <app> resolves the application directory (~/.zhiva/apps/<owner>/<repo> for installed apps, or the current directory for .).
  2. The CLI runs the update check. The engine and dependencies are checked at most once per hour by default; -e 1 -d 1 skips the checks and --update forces them.
  3. The CLI runs bun run start with ZHIVA_ROOT, ZHIVA_APP_ID and a NODE_PATH that includes the application and the global ~/.zhiva/node_modules.
  4. The backend imports base-lib and creates the HTTP server on 127.0.0.1.
  5. apiRouter is mounted at /zhiva-api. Every request must carry the x-zhiva-token header. The token is generated per process with crypto.randomBytes.
  6. oneWindow() starts the native engine. The engine loads the local URL with the token in the zhiva-secret query parameter. Frontend helpers read it and attach the header to requests.
  7. Closing the window ends the process.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
• Full-stack: the CLI runs the start script, the window loads the local server.
  • Static: the CLI runs a built-in static server and then oneWindow(); no application backend exists.
  • URL: the CLI opens the remote URL in a window. No local server is started.

See Application Types.

docs.title: Data directory
docs.text:
~/.zhiva/
├── apps/            # installed applications, <owner>/<repo>
├── bin/zhiva        # CLI symlink
├── master.db/       # Valthera database: installed apps, preferences, cache
├── node_modules/    # shared dependencies, including base-lib
├── scripts/         # cloned Zhiva-scripts repository
├── zhiva(.exe)      # native engine
└── zhiva.nv.txt     # engine version marker

Each application directory may contain .zhiva-port with the last port it used.

docs.title: Install and update flow
docs.text:
• zhiva install owner/repo clones the repository into ~/.zhiva/apps, runs bun install --production, runs the build script when present, records the app in the database and creates shortcuts.
  • Archives are extracted into ~/.zhiva/apps/archive/<name>.
  • zhiva update runs git fetch, compares HEAD with the upstream branch, and for applications with new commits runs git pull, bun install --production and the build script.
  • zhiva self updates the CLI repository, base-lib, the shared dependencies and the engine.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• The API listens on loopback only.
  • Authentication is a per-process random token, delivered to the window through its URL. It protects the local API from other origins, not from other processes running as the same user.
  • Applications are not sandboxed and run with the permissions of the current user.
  • The engine is built with developer tools enabled, which is convenient during development and should be considered when distributing an application.

docs.title: Command-Line Interface (CLI)
docs.text: The zhiva CLI installs, updates and starts applications.

docs.title: Main Commands
docs.text: Command Alias(es) Description start run, startup, o, r Start a Zhiva application. install i, add Install an application from a GitHub repository. create new Create a new application from a template. uninstall rm, remove Uninstall an installed application. list l, ls List installed applications. open link Open a URL in a new Zhiva window. self update-self, self-update Update the zhiva CLI and native engine. update u, up Update all installed Zhiva applications. guess find Find an application by its name using fuzzy search. search s Search the registry for applications. cdf create-desktop-file Create desktop shortcuts for an installed app. db Interact with the Zhiva database. protocol Handle zhiva:// links. doctor Check the Zhiva installation. version --version, -v Show version information. help h Show the help message.

docs.title: start
docs.text:
Starts a Zhiva application.

zhiva start <app-name>

The <app-name> is always based on its GitHub repository path in the format user/repo. However, as a shortcut for the primary developer's apps (wxn0brP), you can omit the username.

Use . to start the application in the current directory.

Examples: 

# Start an app from another user
zhiva start some-user/their-cool-app

# Start one of the primary developer's apps (shortcut)
zhiva start Zhiva-store-app

# Start the project in the current directory
zhiva start .

By default the engine and dependencies are checked for updates at most once per hour. Use -e 1 and -d 1 to disable those checks, or -u to force an update now.

  • -e, --engine <mode>: Controls the update check for the native engine (0: auto, at most once per hour, 1: skip, 2: force).
  • -d, --deps <mode>: Controls the update check for dependencies (0: auto, at most once per hour, 1: skip, 2: force).
  • -u, --update: Forces the engine and dependency update (-e 2 -d 2).

docs.title: install
docs.text:
Installs an application from a GitHub repository or an archive.

zhiva install <app-name-or-repo>
zhiva install ./my-app.zip

Like the start command, the app name is based on the user/repo path.

Archives are installed under archive/<file-name>. When the name cannot be derived from the file name, pass it with -n <name>.

Examples: 

# Install an app from another user
zhiva install some-user/their-cool-app

# Install an app from the primary developer (wxn0brP)
# This is equivalent to 'zhiva install wxn0brP/Zhiva-store-app'
zhiva install Zhiva-store-app

# Install a local archive
zhiva install ./my-app.zip

The install command clones the repository into ~/.zhiva/apps, installs its dependencies using bun install, runs the build script if defined in package.json, and can create desktop shortcuts.

docs.title: create
docs.text:
Creates a new application from the template.

zhiva create [name]

The command clones the official template, removes its git history, sets the metadata in package.json and zhiva.json, replaces the [YOUR NAME], [YOUR APP NAME] and [YEAR] placeholders, points the "Install via Zhiva" badge in the README at the new repository, and installs dependencies.

When the name is omitted and the command runs in a terminal, it asks for the application directory first. When no metadata flags are passed, it then asks for the display name, author and description. If any of --author, --display-name or --description is passed, the command runs without questions.

Options: - -t, --template <url>: Use another template repository. - -a, --author <name>: Author name. Defaults to git config user.name. - --display-name <name>: Display name. Defaults to a name derived from the directory. - --description <text>: Description. Defaults to the display name. - --no-install: Skip dependency installation. - --no-input: Do not ask questions, use defaults.

Examples: 

zhiva create my-app
zhiva create my-app --author wxn0brP --description "My first app"
zhiva create my-app --no-input
zhiva create my-app --template /path/to/local/template
cd my-app
bun run build
zhiva start .

A local template must be a Git repository. git clone copies commits, not uncommitted changes, so commit the template first or create a temporary repository with the files you want.

docs.title: uninstall
docs.text:
Removes a previously installed application.

zhiva uninstall <app-name>

docs.title: list
docs.text:
Lists all applications installed on your system.

zhiva list
zhiva list --json

--json prints an array of application names.

docs.title: update
docs.text:
Updates all installed Zhiva applications by pulling the latest changes from their respective Git repositories.

zhiva update
zhiva update --json

--json prints a map of application names to true (update available) or false (up to date) and does not modify anything.

docs.title: self
docs.text:
Updates the Zhiva framework itself, including the zhiva CLI, the shared base-lib and the native engine.

zhiva self

docs.title: search
docs.text:
Searches the registry for applications. Without arguments it lists every application.

zhiva search
zhiva search store

Options: - --json: Print the result as JSON. - --pretty: Print the JSON result with indentation.

Each entry contains the repository name, description, star count and verification status.

docs.title: guess
docs.text:
Finds installed applications by name using fuzzy matching. Without arguments it lists every installed application.

zhiva guess
zhiva guess store

docs.title: cdf
docs.text:
Creates desktop shortcuts for an installed application.

zhiva cdf <app-name> [flags]

Flags: - d: create a desktop shortcut - m: create a menu entry

Defaults to dm when no flags are given.

Examples: 

zhiva cdf Zhiva-store-app d
zhiva cdf username/repo dm

docs.title: db
docs.text:
Low-level access to the Valthera database in ~/.zhiva/master.db. The first argument is collection.method; JSON5 objects and arrays are parsed.

zhiva db apps.find
zhiva db pref.find

The result is printed as JSON. The command is meant for debugging, not for application code.

docs.title: protocol
docs.text:
Handles zhiva:// links on Linux. It is registered as a desktop protocol handler by the installer and is normally called by the system, not by hand.

Supported commands:

  • zhiva://start/<app>
  • zhiva://install/<app>
  • zhiva://install+start/<app>
  • zhiva://open/<url>
zhiva protocol zhiva://start/Zhiva-store-app

docs.title: doctor
docs.text:
Checks the installation and prints one line per check with a suggested fix for failures.

zhiva doctor

It verifies Bun, Git, WebKitGTK, GTK 3, xdg-utils, the zhiva:// handler, PATH, the native engine, base-lib and the database. On Windows it also checks the zhiva.cmd launcher, WebView2 and the registry protocol handler. The command exits with code 1 when a required component is missing.

docs.title: version
docs.text:
Shows the CLI version (or the git commit when no version is set), the engine version, the Bun version and the Zhiva root directory.

zhiva version
zhiva --version
zhiva version --json

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 Success 1 The command failed, or zhiva doctor found a missing component

Errors are printed to stderr. Commands that offer --json print machine-readable output to stdout without colors.

docs.title: Configuration: zhiva.json
docs.text: zhiva.json describes an application: its metadata, how it is installed, and how it is served. It must be in the repository root. The schema requires name; everything else is optional.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
    "name": "My Awesome App",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "description": "What the app does",
    "author": "your-github-name",
    "license": "MIT",
    "branch": "main",
    "shortcut": "md",
    "icon": "./assets/icon.png",
    "win_icon": "./assets/icon.ico",
    "forcePort": 8081,
    "static": {
        "dirs": {
            "/": "./public",
            "-/": "./dist",
            "/assets": "./dist/assets"
        },
        "files": {
            "/config.js": "./src/config.js"
        },
        "redirects": {
            "/old": "/new"
        },
        "vars": {
            "layout": "public/layout.html"
        }
    }
}

Do not combine static with url. Use either one, or neither for a full-stack application. See Application Types.

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text: Field Type Description name string Required. Display name, used for shortcuts and window titles version string Application version, informational description string Short description author string Author name license string License identifier, e.g. MIT

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Field Type Description branch string Branch to clone and track. Defaults to the repository default branch redirect_repo owner/repository New location when the repository moves redirect_zhiva path/to/zhiva.json#branch Location of the manifest, when it is not in the repository root shortcut d, m, dm, md Where to create shortcuts: desktop, menu or both icon string PNG icon for Linux and macOS. Local path or HTTP URL win_icon string ICO icon for Windows. Local path or HTTP URL

Icons given as URLs are downloaded into the application directory during installation.

To install without any shortcut, pass -s n to zhiva install. The value is not stored in zhiva.json, because the schema only accepts d, m, dm and md.

docs.title: Runtime
docs.text:
Field Type Description forcePort number Preferred backend port. Takes precedence over ZHIVA_PORT url string Load a remote URL instead of a local server static object Serve static files instead of running a backend

If the preferred port is taken, the server falls back to a random free port. The port actually used is written to .zhiva-port in the application directory.

docs.title: static
docs.text:
Field Description dirs URL path to directory mapping. Defaults to { "/": "." } files URL path to single-file mapping redirects URL path to redirect target vars Falcon Frame variables passed to the static server

A leading - in a dirs key lets several directories share the same URL root; the dashes are stripped before serving.

docs.title: Placeholders in the template
docs.text:
The official template ships placeholders instead of real values:

Placeholder Replaced with [YOUR NAME] author [YOUR APP NAME] application name [YEAR] current year

zhiva create fills them in package.json, zhiva.json, LICENSE and the README. When you clone the template manually, replace them by hand.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
The official schema is zhiva.schema.json. It uses JSON Schema draft-07 and rejects unknown fields.

For autocompletion and validation in VS Code, add this to your user or workspace settings.json:

"json.schemas": [
    {
        "fileMatch": ["zhiva.json"],
        "url": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wxn0brP/Zhiva/master/zhiva.schema.json"
    }
]

docs.title: Environment overrides
docs.text: Variable Effect ZHIVA_PORT Preferred port, lower priority than forcePort ZHIVA_ROOT Zhiva data directory, default ~/.zhiva ZHIVA_ENGINE Path to the native engine binary ZHIVA_ASSETS Path to shared base-lib assets

docs.title: Development
docs.text: This page describes the day-to-day workflow of a Zhiva application: running it, rebuilding the frontend, adding API endpoints and debugging.

docs.title: Project
docs.text: This page assumes the project already exists. See Getting Started for zhiva create, the template layout and the build command.

docs.title: Run the application
docs.text:
zhiva start .

The command runs the start script from package.json (the backend) and opens the window when the server is ready. Backend logs are printed to this terminal.

Press Ctrl+C in the terminal or close the window to stop the application.

docs.title: Build loop
docs.text:
The backend runs TypeScript directly, so src/index.ts changes require only a restart. The frontend has to be rebuilt:

  1. change src/browser.ts,
  2. run bun run build,
  3. restart the application.

For automatic rebuilds, the template ships a suglite.json5 file:

{
    cmd: "bun run build",
    watch: ["src"],
}

If you use suglite, run suglite in a second terminal. Other tools work the same way: point them at src and run the build script.

Restart the application after a rebuild. The window keeps the JavaScript it loaded at startup.

docs.title: Add an API endpoint
docs.text:
Define the route in src/index.ts:

import { app, oneWindow } from "@wxn0brp/zhiva-base-lib/server";
import { apiRouter } from "@wxn0brp/zhiva-base-lib/api";

app.static("public");
app.static("dist");

apiRouter.get("/notes", async () => {
    return { err: false, notes: [] };
});

apiRouter.post("/notes", async req => {
    return { err: false, note: req.body };
});

oneWindow();

Call it from src/browser.ts:

import { fetchApiJson, fetchApiPost } from "@wxn0brp/zhiva-base-lib/front/api";

interface NotesResponse {
    err: boolean;
    notes: string[];
}

const data = await fetchApiJson<NotesResponse>("notes");
const created = await fetchApiPost<NotesResponse>("notes", { text: "hello" });

fetchApiJson calls /zhiva-api/notes and adds the authentication token automatically. A shared type imported by both files keeps the backend and frontend in sync:

// src/types.ts
export interface Note {
    id: string;
    text: string;
}

See API Reference for the full backend and frontend API.

docs.title: Static assets
docs.text:
app.static("public") serves public/ at /, and app.static("dist") serves dist/ at /. Both are called in the template. For a layout shared by pages, use Falcon Frame variables:

app.setVar("layout", "public/layout.html");

Static-only applications do not need any of this; see Application Types.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• Backend output: run the application from a terminal with zhiva start .. Output from console.log, errors and stack traces appear there.
  • Installed applications: start them from a terminal with zhiva start <app-name>; shortcuts hide the terminal.
  • Environment: see Troubleshooting for the environment check, port issues and missing libraries.
  • Developer tools: the native engine is built with WebKit/WebView developer tools enabled.
  • Port: the chosen port is written to .zhiva-port in the application directory. If it is taken, the server falls back to a random port.

docs.title: Browser preview
docs.text: Opening the frontend in a regular browser works only for static content. There is no window object and no zhiva-secret token, so fetchApi calls return 401. For previewing API-driven apps, mock the endpoints in development, as the store does in apps/store/src/ui/api-mock.ts.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Purpose ZHIVA_ROOT Zhiva data directory, default ~/.zhiva ZHIVA_PORT Preferred backend port ZHIVA_ENGINE Path to the native engine binary ZHIVA_ASSETS Path to the shared base-lib assets ZHIVA_DEVELOPMENT_DISABLE_SECURE_TOKEN Disables API authentication. Development only, never in a distributed application.

forcePort in zhiva.json takes precedence over ZHIVA_PORT.

docs.text:
• API Reference
  • Configuration
  • Publishing
  • Troubleshooting

docs.title: Getting Started with Zhiva
docs.text: Install Zhiva, create an application, build the frontend and run it.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install instructions

After installation, you will have the zhiva command available in your terminal.

docs.title: Creating Your First Application
docs.text: The easiest way to start a new Zhiva application is the create command, which uses the official template.

docs.title: 1. Create the Project
docs.text:
zhiva create my-awesome-app
cd my-awesome-app

The command clones the template, removes its git history, sets the metadata in package.json and zhiva.json, and installs dependencies. In a terminal it asks for the directory, display name, author and description; pass --author, --display-name and --description (or --no-input) to skip the questions.

docs.title: 2. Understand the Project Structure
docs.text:
The template provides a standard structure for a full-stack Zhiva application:

my-awesome-app/
├── src/
│   ├── index.ts         # Backend entry point (runs in Bun)
│   └── browser.ts       # Frontend entry point (runs in the webview)
├── public/
│   └── index.html       # The main HTML file for your UI
├── dist/                # (Generated) Compiled frontend code
├── package.json         # Project dependencies and scripts
├── suglite.json5        # Watch configuration for suglite
└── zhiva.json           # Zhiva-specific application manifest
  • src/index.ts: This is your server-side code. You'll set up your static file serving and API endpoints here.
  • src/browser.ts: This is your client-side code. All your frontend logic goes here.
  • public/index.html: The webview loads this file, which then loads your compiled browser.ts script.

docs.title: 3. Build the Frontend
docs.text:
zhiva create already installed the dependencies. Rebuild the frontend after changing src/browser.ts:

# Build the frontend
bun run build

The build command (defined in package.json) compiles src/browser.ts and places the output in the dist/ directory.

docs.title: Automatic rebuilds with suglite
docs.text:
The template ships a suglite.json5 file:

{
    cmd: "bun run build",
    watch: ["src"],
}

If you have suglite installed, run it in a second terminal next to zhiva start .. It watches src, runs bun run build after every change and prints the output. Restart the application after a rebuild: the window keeps the JavaScript it loaded at startup.

Any other watcher works too; point it at src and run the build script.

docs.title: 4. Run the Application
docs.text:
You can now run your application using the zhiva CLI:

zhiva start .

# Or

bun run start

This will execute the start script in your package.json (which runs src/index.ts), launch the native window, and load your application.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Development: build loop, adding API routes, debugging, environment variables.
  • API Reference: backend and frontend APIs.
  • Configuration: every zhiva.json field.
  • Publishing: distributing an application and the store.
  • Troubleshooting: when something does not start.

docs.title: Zhiva Install Instruction
docs.text: Zhiva runs on Windows and Linux. The macOS build exists but is untested on real hardware.

docs.title: Linux
docs.text:
• Git
  • Bun: the installer can install it for you
  • WebKitGTK 4.1 and GTK 3: required by the native window
  • xdg-utils: required for desktop shortcuts and the zhiva:// protocol

Install the native dependencies for your distribution:

# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt install libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0 libgtk-3-0 xdg-utils

# Fedora
sudo dnf install webkit2gtk4.1 gtk3 xdg-utils

# Arch
sudo pacman -S webkit2gtk-4.1 gtk3 xdg-utils

# openSUSE
sudo zypper install libwebkit2gtk-4_1-0 libgtk-3-0 xdg-utils

If WebKitGTK is missing, Zhiva still runs, but applications open in your browser instead of a native window.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
• WebView2 runtime: included in Windows 11 and most Windows 10 installs
  • Zhiva Store Auto Install

Repository: https://github.com/wxn0brP/Zhiva-windows

docs.title: Install on Linux
docs.text:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wxn0brP/Zhiva/HEAD/install/prepare.sh | bash
export PATH="$HOME/.zhiva/bin:$PATH"

The installer checks for Git, WebKitGTK and xdg-utils, installs Bun when it is missing, and runs zhiva doctor at the end. At that point ~/.zhiva/bin is not in PATH yet, so the check may report the command as missing; export the directory as shown below.

Add the following to your .bashrc or .zshrc so zhiva is available in new shells:

export PATH="$HOME/.zhiva/bin:$PATH"

If you use zsh, add the following to your .zshrc to enable auto-completion:

[ -s "$HOME/.zhiva/scripts/_zhiva" ] && source "$HOME/.zhiva/scripts/_zhiva"

docs.title: Install your first application
docs.text:
zhiva install Zhiva-store-app
zhiva start Zhiva-store-app

docs.title: Verify the installation
docs.text:
zhiva doctor

doctor checks Bun, Git, WebKitGTK, GTK 3, xdg-utils, the zhiva:// protocol handler, the zhiva command in PATH, the native engine, base-lib and the local database. On Windows it also checks the zhiva.cmd launcher, the WebView2 runtime and the registry protocol handler. Every failed check includes a suggested fix.

zhiva version shows the CLI commit, engine version, Bun version and the Zhiva root directory.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Installation problems, including WebKitGTK, PATH and the zhiva:// protocol, are covered in Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Getting Started: create and run the first application.
  • Development: the development workflow.
  • Troubleshooting: common problems.

docs.title: Publishing an Application
docs.text: A Zhiva application is a normal Git repository. There is no package registry and no publish step: users install it directly from the repository.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
1. zhiva.json exists in the repository root and contains a name.
  2. package.json has a start script, unless the application is static or URL-based.
  3. bun install and bun run build work from a clean clone.
  4. zhiva start . opens the application without errors.
  5. The repository is public and contains the files the app needs at runtime.
  6. The repository has the Zhiva-app topic.

docs.title: Minimal zhiva.json
docs.text:
{
    "name": "My App",
    "description": "What the app does",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "author": "your-github-name",
    "license": "MIT",
    "icon": "./assets/icon.png",
    "win_icon": "./assets/icon.ico"
}

name is the display name used for shortcuts. description, version, author and license are informational. See Configuration for every field.

Icons can be local paths or HTTP URLs. URLs are downloaded during installation.

docs.title: Test the installation path
docs.text:
Before publishing, install your own application the way a user would:

zhiva install your-name/your-app
zhiva start your-name/your-app

This checks that the repository is complete, that the start script works and that shortcuts are created correctly.

docs.title: Discovery in the store
docs.text:
The store and zhiva search query the GitHub search API for repositories with the Zhiva-app topic:

https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=topic:Zhiva-app

Add the topic in the repository settings on GitHub. The store displays the repository description and star count from GitHub.

The search API allows 10 unauthenticated requests per minute per IP. The store reports the rate limit as an error instead of showing an empty list.

docs.title: Verified and banned lists
docs.text:
The Zhiva registry contains:

  • verified.txt: applications reviewed by the maintainers, marked with a Verified badge,
  • banned.txt: applications hidden from the store.

Both files contain one owner/repository per line. Lines starting with # are comments. Verification is manual. In the store, an unverified application shows a security warning before installation.

docs.title: Install badge
docs.text:
Add the badge to your README:

[![Install via Zhiva](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zhiva-install-blue)](https://wxn0brp.github.io/Zhiva-page/i#app=your-name/your-app)

The #app= parameter is the owner/repository identifier. zhiva create generates this line with the correct values.

docs.title: Updates
docs.text:
Installed applications are updated by pulling from Git:

zhiva update

The command fetches every installed repository, updates the ones with new commits, runs bun install --production and the build script when present.

Useful zhiva.json fields:

  • branch: the branch to track, when it is not the repository default,
  • redirect_repo: owner/new-repository, when the repository moves,
  • redirect_zhiva: path/to/zhiva.json#branch, when the manifest lives elsewhere.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
There is no central version registry. version in zhiva.json is informational, and the update check compares Git commits. Tag releases if you want to document them, but users receive the latest commit on the tracked branch.

Keep the update path working: if you rename the repository, add redirect_repo before the old name stops resolving, otherwise existing installations will fail to update.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Installing an application runs its code with the permissions of the current user. Zhiva does not sandbox applications. Publish only code you are willing to distribute, and read the source of applications you install.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Start with zhiva doctor. It checks Bun, Git, WebKitGTK, GTK 3, xdg-utils, the protocol handler, PATH, the engine, base-lib and the database, and prints the command that fixes each failed check. The command exits with code 1 when a required component is missing.

zhiva doctor

docs.title: The window does not open, the app opens in the browser
docs.text:
WebKitGTK is missing. The engine cannot start, so Zhiva falls back to the default browser and shows a notification.

Install the native libraries for your distribution:

# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt install libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0 libgtk-3-0 xdg-utils

# Fedora
sudo dnf install webkit2gtk4.1 gtk3 xdg-utils

# Arch
sudo pacman -S webkit2gtk-4.1 gtk3 xdg-utils

# openSUSE
sudo zypper install libwebkit2gtk-4_1-0 libgtk-3-0 xdg-utils

Then run the check again.

docs.title: zhiva: command not found
docs.text:
~/.zhiva/bin is not in PATH. Add it to your shell profile:

export PATH="$HOME/.zhiva/bin:$PATH"

Open a new shell, or source the profile, and run zhiva version.

docs.title: The window is empty or closes immediately
docs.text:
Run the application from a terminal:

zhiva start <app-name>

The backend output, including errors from src/index.ts, is printed there. For an installed application, the shortcut hides this output.

Common causes:

  • the start script in package.json fails,
  • public/index.html is missing,
  • the frontend was not built (bun run build),
  • the port is taken and the window loads a stale instance.

The chosen port is stored in .zhiva-port in the application directory.

docs.title: Port already in use
docs.text:
Set a fixed port in zhiva.json:

{ "forcePort": 8081 }

or start with ZHIVA_PORT=8081 zhiva start .. If the port is taken, the server falls back to a random free port; the value in .zhiva-port is updated.

docs.title: zhiva:// links do nothing
docs.text:
The protocol handler is not registered. Check it with:

xdg-mime query default x-scheme-handler/zhiva

Register it again:

xdg-mime default zhiva-protocol.desktop x-scheme-handler/zhiva

xdg-utils must be installed. Re-running the installer also restores the handler.

docs.title: The store is empty or shows an error
docs.text:
The store loads its list from the GitHub search API, which allows 10 unauthenticated requests per minute per IP. When the limit is hit, the store shows Could not load applications instead of a list. Wait a minute and reload.

If you are offline, the store reports that too. The rest of the CLI works offline for installed applications.

docs.title: install says the app is not valid
docs.text: Every application must contain zhiva.json in its repository root, and the repository must be a normal Git repository. Check that the repository is not empty and that zhiva.json is committed.

docs.title: zhiva install ./file.zip asks for a name
docs.text:
The name is derived from the archive file name. If the file name is not usable, pass it explicitly:

zhiva install ./file.zip -n my-app

Supported formats: .zip, .tar.gz, .tar.bz2, .tar.xz, .7z. The matching tool must be available. On Windows, .zip uses unzip when present, otherwise tar or PowerShell Expand-Archive; .7z requires 7-Zip.

docs.title: Updates behave unexpectedly
docs.text:
zhiva start checks the engine and dependencies at most once per hour. Control it with:

zhiva start . -e 1 -d 1      # skip engine and dependency checks
zhiva start . --update       # force both
zhiva self                   # update the CLI, base-lib and engine

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
The Windows installer installs Git and Bun when they are missing, adds %USERPROFILE%\.zhiva\bin to the user PATH, creates the zhiva.cmd launcher and registers zhiva:// links.

zhiva is not recognized

The PATH change applies to new terminals. Close and reopen the terminal.

Shortcuts do nothing, or zhiva:// links do not open

The installer creates %USERPROFILE%\.zhiva\bin\zhiva.cmd and the zhiva:// registry entry. If either is missing, for example after a manual setup, re-run the Windows installer. The environment check reports both as launcher and protocol handler.

The window does not open

The WebView2 runtime is missing. The environment check reports it as webview2. Install the Evergreen WebView2 runtime and run the check again.

Installing an application fails at the clone step

Git is required. The Windows installer provides it; after a manual setup, install Git for Windows and reopen the terminal. zhiva install reports the missing dependency before it tries to clone.

docs.title: macOS
docs.text: The macOS build exists but is untested on real hardware. Windows and Linux are the supported platforms.

docs.title: Still stuck
docs.text:
1. zhiva version
  2. run the app from a terminal and copy the output
  3. open an issue at github.com/wxn0brP/Zhiva/issues with the environment check output and the application logs
